entries.name: Axe (one-handed)
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 198 (Quaternius static Axe via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Axe_Small.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword entry). The pack has three axes: Axe (crescent battle-axe head with a top spike), Axe_Double (two-bladed labrys) and Axe_Small (a bearded one-handed axe); Axe_Small was taken because its single broad bearded head is the plainest axe silhouette and reads at a glance in the hero view. Height 0.75 m is the whole axe, heel to the top of the poll (a one-handed axe; the head is chunky for its size, about 0.30 m from poll to edge, as the stylized source draws it). Rest pose: upright, haft along +Y, heel on y = 0; head flat in the XY plane with the cutting edge toward +X (about 4-6 cm thick along Z). The pipeline centres the bounding box, so the haft is not on the origin: the haft axis runs at x = -0.115 m, z = 0 (its curved heel ends near x = -0.10 m). Grip (cord-wrapped) from y 0.19 to 0.43 m, hold at about y 0.27 m; bare flared heel 0 to 0.19 m; steel collar 0.52 m; head from y 0.37 (beard tip) to 0.73 m, steel poll cap 0.56 to 0.75 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by (+0.115, -0.27, 0) m in the axe's frame, then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and +X (the edge) faces the swing. Colours match the sword: head, poll and collar pale steel (moon over sky), haft amber over sky.

entries.name: Cloud
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, rounded multi-lobed cumulus (Quaternius 2021)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static cloud on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge, and the Ultimate Nature Pack used for the trees has no cloud. This is Cloud_2 from Quaternius's Ultimate Platformer Pack on itch.io (free download; License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0). Of the pack's three clouds (all rendered) it reads best as a puffy cumulus: a big central lobe with a smaller puff on each side over a flat base, the classic anime cloud profile, where Cloud_1 is two lumps and Cloud_3 a long sloping mound. The broad side faces +Z (the front view shows the three lobes); y = 0 is the flat bottom. Size: a sky prop, 15 m tall, about 25 m wide and 15 m deep; real cumulus are hundreds of metres across, so a film places it far off or scales it (uniform scale keeps the base flat). Colours on indigo: sclera white shading to moon pale blue, with ink. noInk was tried too: without the hull the lobes merge into one white blob and the cloud reads as a lump, so the ink stays (it also draws the creases between puffs). Shade threshold 0 (default 0.35): at the default half the cloud went blue in patches; at 0 the shade sits on the underside and the far side, the flat-bottomed anime cumulus look. Smooth shading kept so the shade falls as soft bands. Static: no clips.

entries.name: Dagger
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 202 (Quaternius static Dagger via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Dagger_2.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries). Height 0.35 m is the whole dagger, pommel to tip. Rest pose: upright, tip at +Y, pommel on y = 0; blade flat in the XY plane (edges along X, about 2.5 cm wide, crossguard about 7 cm wide along X, 3 cm thick along Z); symmetric, so the blade axis is on x = z = 0 (the model origin is the pommel's bottom centre). Pommel 0 to 0.03 m, cord-wrapped grip from y 0.03 to 0.135 m (hold at about y 0.085 m), crossguard 0.135 to 0.165 m, blade 0.16 to 0.35 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by -0.085 m along the dagger's Y, then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction (or against it for a reverse grip). Colours match the sword and axe: blade pale steel (moon over sky), grip amber over sky, crossguard and pommel gold over sky (gold threshold -0.1 so the small guard reads gold, not shade, from the front).

entries.style: low-poly chibi, painted texture flattened to flat colours (Quaternius 2020)

source.author: Quaternius

The pack has two demons; both were rendered and the red Demon was chosen over the GreenDemon: red skin, fangs in an open mouth, striped horns and bat ears read as an oni, while the green one is a plain bull-horned blob with a worried face. Its .blend expects Demon_Texture.png beside itself; the pipeline relinks it from the zip's Textures folder. The painted texture is flattened to 16 clusters: the eleven reds (skin, mouth cavity, nose, chin tuft, cheek patches) -> body; the near-black cluster (eye discs, brows, ear insides) -> dark; the cream cluster (horns, fangs and the eye catchlights, which fall in it) and the untextured #e7e7e7 -> horn; the two olive-brown horn stripes -> band; the plum cluster (tongue) -> tongue. dark has threshold -0.6 so the eyes stay mostly solid. entries.name: Mushroom
entries.style: low-poly chibi, painted texture flattened to flat colours (Quaternius 2020)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Not a numbered wave-1 row: an addition from the Textured Cute Monster Pack (Aug 2020) on OpenGameArt, the pack the library already uses for the ghost and demon, as a forest spirit for fantasy and yokai scenes. Its .blend expects Mushroom_Texture.png beside itself; the pipeline relinks it from the zip's Textures folder. The painted texture is flattened to 16 clusters: the five browns (cap top and gills) -> cap; the two creams (cap spots, teeth and the eye catchlights, which fall in the paler one) and the untextured #e7e7e7 -> spot; the five olive greys (the stem body and face) -> body; the near-black cluster (eye discs, mouth rim) and the dark olive cluster (lower eyelids) -> dark; the two plums (mouth cavity and tongue) -> tongue. The source's olive-grey stem and brown cap are recoloured to a pale stem under a vermilion cap with cream spots, so it reads as a toadstool at a glance; the spots are whole faces, so they come out as blocky patches, not round dots. dark has threshold -0.6 so the eyes stay mostly solid. Ground: like the ghost and demon it is a stem-shaped body on a flat base, no legs; Walk and Jump hop off the ground by design (up to 13 and 22 cm), Death sinks up to 11 cm as it tips onto its cap and HitRecieve 2 mm as it rocks, so both clamp to the ground. Height 0.8 m is a chibi choice: a mushroom spirit has no real size, and 0.8 m puts it at a child's height, matching the pack's ghost and demon so they stand together.

entries.name: Scythe
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 203 (Quaternius static Scythe via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Scythe.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries, and their colours, so the weapons read as one set). Height 1.7 m is the whole scythe, the bottom of the hooked snath to the top of its knob (a reaper's / war scythe, about head height on an adult). Rest pose: upright, snath along +Y with a gentle S-curve and a hooked foot on y = 0; blade flat in the XY plane (about 2 cm thick along Z), mounted by a collar at y 1.40 to 1.60 m, curving out toward +X and down to its tip at (+0.46, 1.33) m, with the concave cutting edge facing down toward the user and a short back spike to -X. The pipeline centres the bounding box, so the snath is not on the origin: its axis runs at z = 0 and x = -0.37 m near the foot, -0.28 m at mid grip and about -0.33 m along the bare upper shaft (y 0.85 to 1.40 m). The cord-wrapped grip runs from y 0.10 to 0.80 m. Two-handed hold: lower hand at about (-0.37, 0.25, 0) m, upper hand at about (-0.28, 0.70, 0) m; a one-handed carry (reaper pose) takes the upper hand point. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by minus that hand point in the scythe's frame (e.g. (+0.28, -0.70, 0) m for the upper hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and +X (the blade) points forward over the shoulder or out to the side. Colours match the sword: blade and back spike pale steel (moon over sky), snath, grip wrap and collar amber over sky.

entries.name: Round shield
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius

The pack has two round shields with the same mesh: Shield_Round (plain wood planks) and Shield_Round_2 (the same planks quartered with white paint); Shield_Celtic_Golden was rendered too but is a tall waisted gold-and-gem shield, not round. Shield_Round_2 was taken because the quartered face reads as a shield at a glance in cel, where plain planks become one amber disc. Height 0.7 m is the diameter (a typical 0.6-0.9 m round shield). Rest pose: upright, painted face toward +Z, bottom rim on y = 0, centred on x = 0; a 14-sided steel rim with 8 rivets around a shallow plank dome (front of the dome at z about +0.10 m, board back at z about -0.03 m). Grip: two short vertical wooden handles on the back (-Z side), at x about -0.14 and +0.14 m, from y about 0.25 to 0.49 m, standing out to z about -0.12 m; the shield's centre is at y 0.35 m. To put it on an arm: parent to the forearm/hand so the arm passes through both handles along X (or hold one handle in the fist), with +Z (the face) pointing away from the body. Colours match the sword and axe: rim and rivets pale steel (moon over sky), wood planks amber over sky; the source's white paint is mapped to the script's red accent (paint), since white paint against the pale steel rim lost the quartering. Wood and paint thresholds are 0 so the gently domed face stays lit in the front views.

Height 20 m keel to masthead (the mast tops of a medium sailing ship sit about 20 m up) gives a 21.3 m length bowsprit to stern and a 9.6 m beam (chunky toy proportions, beam about twice a real ship's). y = 0 is the keel; the waterline sits at about y = 1.8 m (the lower hull chine, where the dark underbody band ends), so a film sinks the ship 1.8 m into its water plane. Kenney's black sails with a bone-white skull are kept: tan hull planks, red rails and masts, dark brown sails and pennants (sails and pennants are one-sided, drawn double-sided). Static, no clips.

entries.name: Skeleton Warrior (KayKit)
entries.style: chibi low-poly, hard-surface, gradient atlas flattened (KayKit 2024)

source.author: Kay Lousberg
source.note: Skeleton_Warrior.glb from the pack's GitHub mirror, pinned to commit 15b62b9 (LICENSE.txt: CC0, Kay Lousberg); the gradient atlas is embedded in the GLB. Unlike the Adventurers rigs, this GLB carries no weapons: the pack ships them as separate asset files, so Skeleton_Blade.gltf and Skeleton_Shield_Small_A.gltf (same commit, with their .bin files and skeleton_texture.png) are attached with ingest.attach to handslot.r and handslot.l. 26 of 95 clips kept (1H melee set, block, hits, deaths, the skeleton-only shamble, collapse/resurrect and awaken/spawn clips, taunt, cheer, sit; ranged, 2H, dual-wield, spellcast, lie-down and pose clips dropped). death is Death_A; Death_C_Skeletons (falls apart: the body tumbles about 1.5 m back and one leg is left standing, as authored) and Death_C_Skeletons_Resurrect stay under their own names. Height 1.6 m like the KayKit knight: KayKit characters are chibi (head about a third of the body), so 1.6 m keeps the helmeted skull near a real head size. Colours: the bones stay bone-white as the main read; the grey iron armour and helmet go navy (sky over near-black); the blade is pale steel (moon over near-black) so it reads apart from the navy armour in both tones; the shield has a steel rim and an amber wooden face.

entries.name: Sofa
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Substitutes for the plan's Quaternius sofa (poly.pizza static GLB, blocked by a Cloudflare challenge). Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0 `loungeSofa` (GLB): a three-seat sofa with a rounded back, square arms and short wooden legs. Of the kit's sofas (loungeSofa, loungeSofaLong and loungeSofaCorner: one family, the long and corner pieces are sectional modules; loungeDesignSofa and its corner: a boxier low-back design sofa, 2.16 m wide at the same scale, too big for a small Japanese apartment) this one reads best as a living-room sofa. The cushions (source `carpet`, pale pink) are drawn in the script's red accent, apart from the furniture wood; the legs (`wood`) keep the desk's wood pair. Front (seat) faces +Z. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Spaceship (fighter)
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, painted texture flattened (Quaternius Ultimate Spaceships 2021)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Substitution: plan row 138 is Quaternius "Spaceship" on the poly.pizza CDN (blocked by a Cloudflare challenge). Used the Striker fighter from Quaternius's Ultimate Spaceships pack (May 2021) on OpenGameArt, CC0 per the page; the .blend is used because it carries the packed texture (the FBX and OBJ reference none). Chosen over the pack's Spitfire and Challenger (also rendered) for the sleekest anime-fighter silhouette: twin forward gun prongs, a central canopy and anhedral wings. Real size: a small one-seat fighter about 12 m long, so the rest height (canopy plus antennas) is 3.8 m, giving 11.9 m long and 7.1 m across. The lowest point is the two wing tips, at y = 0. Painted texture flattened to 10 colours; recoloured as a white/blue mecha fighter with a red canopy and gold trim. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Spear
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Plan row 199 (Quaternius static Spear via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Spear.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries). Height 2.0 m is the whole spear, butt to point (a common infantry or hunting spear is 1.8-2.2 m). Rest pose: upright, point at +Y, butt on y = 0; the leaf-shaped head is flat in the XY plane (edges along X, about 0.10 m wide, 2 cm thick along Z). The pipeline centres the bounding box; the shaft axis runs at about x = -0.003 m, z = 0 (the stylized shaft wobbles: it drifts to x = -0.017 m near y 1.0 m and the butt kinks to x = +0.04 m below y 0.1 m). Cord-wrapped lower grip from y 0.16 to 0.60 m (rear hand at about y 0.35 m); bare shaft above it (lead hand for a two-handed thrust at about y 0.95 m, axis x = -0.017 m); a second binding from 1.39 to 1.61 m under the head; steel head 1.61 to 2.00 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by (+0.003, -0.35, 0) m in the spear's frame (or (+0.017, -0.95, 0) for the lead hand), then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction and the point faces the thrust. Colours match the sword and axe: head pale steel (moon over sky), shaft and both cord bindings amber over sky (the bindings read by their ink rings).

The pipeline centres the bbox, not the pole: the pole base (0.52 m square foot) is centred at x = 0, z = -0.9 m, and the arm reaches forward over +Z to the lamp head at z = +1.17 m (yaw 180 so the lamp overhangs the road in front). To stand the pole on a kerb point P, place the model at P + (0, 0, 0.9) in its own frame. Static, no clips.

entries.name: Sushi nigiri (salmon)

entries.style: low-poly, flat colours; an octagonal slice cut-face up: nori band, rice ring, salmon and cucumber filling. The pack models it squat (1.9 : 1), so at a real 0.03 m tall it is 0.057 m across, a futomaki-sized slice rather than a thin hosomaki

source.author: Quaternius

entries.name: Sword (one-handed)
entries.style: low-poly, hard-surface, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius

Height 0.9 m is the whole sword, pommel to tip (an arming sword). Rest pose: upright, tip at +Y, pommel on y = 0; blade flat in the XY plane (edges along X, crossguard about 0.19 m wide along X, 4 cm thick along Z). Grip from y 0.04 to 0.22 m (hold at about y 0.13 m; the model origin is the pommel's bottom centre, on the blade axis), pommel 0 to 0.04 m, crossguard 0.22 to 0.31 m, blade 0.26 to 0.90 m. To put it in a hand: parent to the hand, offset by -0.13 m along the sword's Y, then rotate so Y runs along the fist's thumb direction. Colours: blade, crossguard and pommel pale steel (moon over sky), leather-wrapped grip amber over sky. Unlike the katana it is straight, double-edged, with a wide steel crossguard and no brass.

entries.name: Low table
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0)

source.author: Kenney
source.note: Kenney Furniture Kit 2.0 `tableCoffee` (GLB), not the plan's Quaternius table (poly.pizza only, blocked by a Cloudflare challenge). entries.name: Tree

source.author: Quaternius

Height 7 m: a mature small broadleaf street or park tree (maple, cherry, young oak) is 6-8 m; at 7 m the trunk is about 0.35 m across and the canopy starts at 3 m, so a 1.6 m person stands well under it, as in an anime park or school-yard background. entries.name: Autumn tree
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, clustered faceted crown on a forked white birch trunk (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static tree on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is BirchTree_Autumn_4 from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip as the broadleaf `tree`. Of the ten CommonTree_Autumn and BirchTree_Autumn variants it has the fullest crown and the most tree-like silhouette, and its forked white birch trunk and tall clustered crown read differently from the broadleaf's round CommonTree canopy. Height 9 m: a young silver birch in a park or school yard is 8-12 m; the crown starts at about 3 m. Yaw 90 puts the broad side of the crown (8.3 m wide, 2.9 m deep) to the front. Colours: Paper noon has no gold, so the default script is Indigo moon: gold leaves (practical) shading to amber (iris), the second leaf clusters amber shading to accent red, pale moonlit bark (moon) shading to the sky's navy. Static: no clips.

entries.name: Palm tree
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, curved segmented trunk under a crown of faceted fronds (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static palm tree on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is PalmTree_1 from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip as the tree, tree-pine, tree-autumn and bush entries, so they read as one set. Of the four palms in the pack it has the fullest crown (more than a dozen fronds, 5.2 x 4.7 m) on the classic S-curved coconut-palm trunk; PalmTree_3 is straighter and thinner-crowned, PalmTree_4 has only eight fronds, and PalmTree_2 leans so far that its base sits 3.5 m off the crown's centre. The fronds are closed shells (a doubleSided render was identical), so they are not double-sided. Its Coconuts material is buried in the crown and never shows, so it maps to trunk. Height 8 m: a coconut palm on a beach or resort promenade is 6-10 m when young to mid-age (old ones reach 20-30 m); at 8 m the fronds spring from about 7 m and droop to 5.5 m, high over a 1.6 m person, as in an anime beach or island background. Colours on meadow: fronds the mid green (iris) shading to the deep green (hair), a richer green than the willow's light foliage; the trunk is pale skin-tan shading to vermilion (accent). Meadow has no brown: of its non-green pairs, skin over accent gives the clearest two-tone on the thin trunk and the warmest, closest read of a sun-bleached palm trunk (skin over practical and practical over skin barely separate, and moon over skin is the willow's trunk). The red shade is a little hot up close. Static: no clips.

entries.name: Pine tree
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours, tiered faceted canopy (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan names Quaternius static models on poly.pizza, which is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is PineTree_4 from the same Quaternius Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0) that the broadleaf tree entry uses, so the two read as one set. Of the five PineTree variants it has the leaning, kinked bare trunk and a crown of stacked tiers held high: the silhouette of a Japanese black pine (kuromatsu) at a shrine or on a coast (PineTree_3 is the fuller Christmas-tree conifer). Height 10 m: a mature kuromatsu in a shrine ground, park or coastal windbreak is about 8-15 m (wild ones reach 20+); at 10 m the crown starts near 5 m, so people walk under it, and it stands clearly above the 7 m broadleaf tree. Colours on meadow: the needles are iris (mid green) over hair (deep green), an evergreen crown. Meadow has no brown, so the trunk is skin (warm tan) over accent (red): the warm, reddish bark anime pines are painted with, kept off green so the trunk stays apart from the crown's shade; accent over hair was tried and its green shade side merged with the canopy shadow. Static: no clips.

entries.name: Velociraptor

entries.name: Whale
entries.style: low-poly, flat colours (Quaternius 2018)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: Wave-1 row 38 named the Quaternius Low Poly Sea Animals whale (poly.pizza, behind a Cloudflare challenge; one Swim clip). source.note: Wave-1 row 77 named the Quaternius Worker from the Animated Characters (24-clip rig) set on poly.pizza, now behind a Cloudflare challenge. Substituted with Worker_Male from the Quaternius Ultimate Animated Character Pack (Nov 2019) on OpenGameArt (same zip and pin as man-casual and adventurer): the same character concept (hard hat, vest over a T-shirt, shorts). It ships 11 clips (idle, walk, punch, hit, sit, walk-carry, pick-up, one-handed shoot, victory, defeat, stand-up), not 24: no run, jump, death or gun idles. The source vest is brown and the hat dull gold; both are painted festival amber here so the hard hat and hi-vis read at a glance.
